text:
lee: Proposal — shift from a pure token-bucket per-key to a lightweight 'burst-ticket' layer that grants short-lived burst slots (50–200ms tickets) before falling back to steady-state rate limits. Aims: isolate microbursts, avoid penalizing long-tail steady clients, and keep latency SLOs.
anika: quick q — how are tickets minted? fixed refill or adaptive?
lee: thinking adaptive. baseline bucket still exists. Tickets are issued from a small shared reservoir per-org + per-key cap. Reservoir refills slower (seconds) than token bucket (ms) so it absorbs microbursts without changing long-term throughput.
matt: sounds like a hybrid leaky/token approach. Do we need preemption? e.g., high-priority traffic should be able to grab tickets in emergencies.
sato: for priority: attach small priority weight to tickets. If quota exhausted, higher priority can bump a lower-priority ticket (eviction) but only if it won't violate per-org SLA. Eviction should be rare.
dana: concern — this adds complexity to enforcement path. Any perf numbers?
lee: prototyped in dev cluster: 0.6ms added p50 on enqueue, p99 +1.2ms. Microburst tail (95–99) drop rate reduced by ~70% compared to strict token-bucket.
anika: nice. What about fairness across many small keys in a noisy org? shared reservoir could be monopolized.
sato: plan: hierarchical caps — per-key ticket cap + per-org reservoir + decay window. Also a soft-fairness algorithm: give unused ticket credits back to org after short idle.
matt: telemetry checklist we need for rollout: 1) ticket grant rate (per org/key), 2) eviction events, 3) ticket wait time, 4) fallback to steady-state rate limit, 5) latency impact per priority tier.
dana: add a metric for "ticket-induced throttles" vs normal throttles so we can see if tickets mask real overloads.
lee: good call. UX on console: a new "burst" tab in Quotas page showing current reservoir size, recent grants, and a heatmap of bursty keys. Want to show recommended config to reduce cost.
anika: recommend we also surface alerts when eviction spikes > threshold and a runbook link.
sato: rollout strategy: feature flag per org, start with small internal beta orgs, then opt-in customers, then default-on for low-risk tiers. Canary traffic: 1% of requests routed through ticketing path and mirrored for comparison.
matt: do we need a migration story? e.g., for customers already tuning token buckets.
dana: maybe a knob to set ticket size to 0 (feature off) so defaults don't surprise customers. Also clear changelog.
lee: agree. Also need a durability note: ticket state lives in in-memory faststore (local) with periodic reconciliation to central store. If node dies, tickets for that node are lost — which is fine (degenerates to stricter throttling). Documented in rollout notes.
anika: ops-bot, create alert on disk-backed reconciliation failures and shepherd canary next week? :party-parrot: 
ops-bot: Created incident-channel alert: #canary-burst-ticket-recon, threshold=3 failures in 5m. Assigned to eng-runtime oncall.
sato: next steps: write RFC outlining algorithm, required metrics, and console wireframes. I'll prototype eviction metrics in instrumentation next sprint.
matt: want a short config example for ops to review.
lee: paste config snippet:```
burst_ticketing:
  enabled: true
  per_org_reservoir: 1000
  per_key_cap: 5
  reservoir_refill_secs: 10
  ticket_ttl_ms: 200
  priority_weights:
    high: 2
    normal: 1
    low: 0.5
```
anika: looks sensible. We should also run a chaos test that kills local nodes to ensure graceful degradation.
dana: timeline: RFC this week, telemetry proto next sprint, internal beta in 3 weeks?
lee: yep. I'll draft RFC and ping reviewers. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
